messages:
alex: Heads-up, I'm seeing steady mem growth in long streaming/toolloop runs (~8-24h) on the s-rt-prod pool. Not a spike, just slow upward slope until OOMs.

maria: saw similar on canary yesterday, pegged to sessions with lots of tool calls + intermittent short heartbeats.

chen: what's the metric? RSS or allocator-level? any pmap/heap profile?

alex: RSS + allocator tracked. pmap shows resident climbing ~200MB per 6h on busy workers. Heap-prof shows retained KV pages not reclaimed. quick logs:

alex: ```
# pmap summary snippet
PID   RSS        VSZ
1234  1.9G       6.2G
1235  2.1G       6.2G
# heap-dump top
kv_pages_retained: 4821
kv_frag_bytes: 312MB
```

samir: interesting. does the runtime heartbeat (slot liveness) align with the eviction window? we recently tweaked heartbeat interval for toolloops to reduce noise.

alex: exactly my suspicion. toolloop heartbeat became adaptive (backoff when inactive) which introduced 10-90s jitter. eviction window still expects steady 30s cadence, so some slots cross the threshold and get enqueued for eviction while still referenced by in-flight toolloop iterations. eviction marks page, but reuse path has a race so page ends up pinned in a partial list -> fragmentation.

maria: repro steps? can we force jitter on canary and capture traces?

alex: I ran a local stress: start long chat -> spawn toolloop with 100 quick tools, intermittent sleeps. When heartbeat jitter >40s we see "kv_evict_enqueue" logs followed by "kv_pin_failed" traces. snippet: ```
[2026-03-16T10:12:03Z] kv_evict_enqueue slot=0x7f... reason=idle_threshold
[2026-03-16T10:12:04Z] kv_pin_failed slot=0x7f... ref=1 owner=toolloop-91
[2026-03-16T10:12:05Z] kv_unused_fragment ++size=64KB pool=slabA
```

chen: @alex can you attach full trace/artifact? also which PR changed heartbeat?

alex: pushing trace to the artifacts bucket now: s3://redwood-artifacts/kv-heartbeat/2145678901/trace.tar.gz
PR is #4128 (adaptive-heartbeat-toolloops) by @taylan — reverted in prod last week but canary still had it.

samir: possible fixes: 1) make eviction window tolerant to jitter (longer grace) 2) ensure eviction handshake checks in-flight refs before finalizing 3) revert adaptive heartbeat on toolloops and re-evaluate.

maria: for short-term mitigation, we should add a DCHECK: if a slot gets enqueued for eviction and then has inbound pin requests within X secs, cancel eviction. cheap guard.

alex: agree. I can prototype (2) this afternoon: add a small backoff window where enqueue->finalize requires a stable idle check. If pin arrives, clear. Should fix pinned fragments quickly.

chen: also let's add a perf-test that simulates adaptive jitter and asserts stable RSS over 12h. add to long-run CI.

samir: assigned: alex->prototype patch, chen->test harness, maria->canary rollout coord. I'll open a follow-up issue with timeline.

infra-bot: deploy event: canary cluster redeployed with adaptive-heartbeat reverted at 2026-03-16T13:30:22Z :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks. I'll post the PR link when ready. expected diff small in kv/evict.cc to make finalize idempotent.

maria: also add metric kv_eviction_aborts and kv_pin_race_count so we can alert if this reoccurs.

alex: good call. logging plan: increment kv_eviction_aborts when we cancel finalize, kv_pin_race_count when we observe pin during eviction. set alert threshold 50/hour for now.

samir: final note: this explains why long-context streaming + toolloops were worst-case — lots of intermittent activity creates heartbeat jitter and makes eviction churn fragment memory over time. root cause non-obvious but patchable.

alex: PR: #4192 (WIP) - prototype guard and metrics. Will request reviews from chen/maria.

chen: ack, will add CI harness today.

maria: thanks all. update in this thread when PR is up or if canary shows regressions. :thumbsup:
